status_note: REFERENCED (2026-09-01) — shipped to the public catalog. Block 2 of the 3-block Engine Builder arc: volume expansion + threshold-dominant middle intensity. Assumes Block 1 completed OR an equivalent aerobic base declared at intake. Not yet REVIEWED: no domain-specialist audit, so `reviewed_by` / `review_evidence[]` are deliberately absent.

goals.primary_intent: Threshold expansion. Block 2 is where the majority of VO2max and LT2 (lactate threshold 2) gains land — two hard sessions per week on top of a Z1 volume floor higher than Block 1's. This is not a base block; the base is assumed. If it isn't there, Block 1 first.

arc.block_2_volume: 8-12 weeks — this program. Two hard sessions per week — a threshold session + a Norwegian 4×4 — layered on top of the Block 1 volume ceiling. Threshold cruise duration expands from 3×8 → 3×15 minutes across the block. VO2max session variants alternate (4×4 vs 5×3 shorter-interval per Rønnestad-style block).
arc.block_3_polarise: 12-16 weeks — expected. 80/20 polarised model, race-specific work, taper and test.
arc.note: Block 2 is the sharp-end block. Users who did Block 1 and want to keep going should expect the next 8-12 weeks to be harder in absolute terms (more time, more intensity) even though the shape is familiar.

block_2_targets.note: Expected ranges for a user who completed Block 1 and moves into Block 2. Users starting Block 2 without a base will underperform these ranges — the pre-req check at intake exists to catch that.

modality_policy.primary_modality: Whatever the user carried through Block 1 (row, bike, ski-erg, run). Block 2 does not change modality.
modality_policy.cross_modal: Users can substitute a Z1 session on a different modality; hard sessions stay on the declared modality (specificity of adaptation — Joyner & Coyle 2008).

concurrent_strength_policy.recommendation: MAINTENANCE ONLY — same rules as Block 1, but tighter monitoring.
rules: 2-3 strength sessions per week, no more.
RPE cap of 7. No PR attempts, no top-set AMRAPs, no failure.
6+ hours separation from any hard cardio session on the same day (Robineau 2016 dose-response).
If both must share a day, do the strength session first (Eddens 2018 +6.91% lower-body strength).
Skip the strength session on Norwegian 4×4 days; skip the following day's lower-body strength session too if the 4×4 hit high load.
If the two hard cardio sessions of the week land Tuesday + Friday, do lower-body strength Sunday only.
concurrent_strength_policy.rationale: Block 2 accumulates more endurance volume + more high-intensity work than Block 1. Fyfe 2016 showed endurance VOLUME (not intensity) drives interference. Wilson & Loenneke 2012 meta: interference is largest when endurance sessions are hard and frequent. Schumann 2022 SMD -0.28 on explosive strength survives here — the loss zone is bigger in Block 2 than Block 1. Practical translation: an 8-12 week volume block is still not the block to chase a squat PR.

principles.rule: Two hard sessions per week — a threshold session + a VO2max session. Never three.
principles.detail: Seiler 2010 polarised distribution: 20% hard at most. A third hard session pushes the block into an over-reach the recovery capacity of Block 2 users doesn't support. Ronnestad 2020 short-vs-long interval comparison uses two hard sessions/week — the standard reference.

principles.rule: The threshold session is Block 2's primary driver. It expands 3×8 → 3×15 min across the block.
principles.detail: LT2 (MLSS) shift is the single biggest performance lever for endurance events lasting 20-90 min (Joyner & Coyle 2008). Threshold sessions produce more time-in-zone than 4×4 and drive MCT1 upregulation (Pilegaard 2000). Block 2 leans into it.

principles.rule: The second hard session alternates 4×4 and short-interval (5×3 or 8×2) per week
principles.detail: Ronnestad & Hansen 2020 comparison: short intervals accumulate more time-at-VO2max per session for well-trained users; long intervals produce comparable adaptation with less monotony. Alternating avoids the plateau either format shows in isolation. Bishop 2008 repeated-sprint literature supports periodic short-interval work as VO2max complement.

principles.rule: Z1 volume floor rises across the block — week 1 baseline, week 4 +15%, week 8 +30%
principles.detail: Bishop 2019 volume-vs-intensity synthesis: volume drives mitochondrial content beyond a threshold; intensity drives peak capacity. Block 2 stacks volume + intensity. The Z1 volume floor increase is what makes the two hard sessions/week sustainable — without it, the interval work runs on fumes.

principles.rule: If the user is running, the mileage ramp is capped at ≤10%/week
principles.detail: Nielsen 2014 running-injury dose-response literature: sudden mileage jumps drive running-related injury. Block 2 tempts users to ramp both intensity and mileage; the cap resists that.

principles.rule: Threshold retest (20-min TT or 30-min TT for run) at week 4 + week 8-12 is the primary measurement
principles.detail: Threshold pace / power is where Block 2 progress shows up. VO2max is a slower-moving needle. Rest HR + submax HR still tracked but are not the KPI here.

questions.label: Did you complete Engine Builder Block 1 (or a comparable 8-week aerobic base) within the last 4 weeks?
questions.help: Block 2 assumes a base. Without one, you'll under-adapt and over-fatigue. If you finished Block 1 recently, this is the natural next step.

options.label: Yes — I finished Block 1 (or equivalent base) within the last 4 weeks
Yes, but more than 4 weeks ago
No, but I have an equivalent aerobic base (5+ hrs/week cardio, can hold Z1 for 75+ min)
options.hint: Straight into Block 2 with declaration checkpoint

options.label: No — I haven't done a structured aerobic block

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Block 2 needs 4 minimum. Two hard sessions + two Z1 + optionally a fifth easy day.

options.label: 3 days
options.hint: Below the block's evidence-backed floor. Program will warn.

questions.label: How many hours of cardio per week are you doing right now?
questions.help: Only count sessions where HR was elevated for 20+ min continuously.

questions.label: Which modality do you want to sharpen in Block 2?
questions.help: Block 2 does not change modality mid-block. Whatever you pick here, stay on for hard sessions.

questions.label: Peak HR you saw during Block 1's Norwegian 4×4 (approximate, from a chest strap if you had one).
questions.help: Used to personalise the Block 2 hard-session HR targets. If unknown, we'll use HUNT formula.

questions.label: Submax HR at fixed pace: how much did it drop from Block 1 intake to Block 1 retest?
questions.help: Negative number = drop = good. If < -5 bpm, you're a Push tier candidate.

questions.label: Best 20-minute effort in the last 4 weeks — pace (min/km), power (W), or split (min:sec /500m).
questions.help: Free text. Used to set the initial threshold-cruise target. If you haven't done one, week 1 has a 20-min TT to establish baseline.

questions.label: Any joint or tendon issues flaring right now?
questions.help: Achilles, patellar, hip, low back. Free text — surfaces before hard sessions as a reminder.

questions.label: How many strength sessions per week are you doing / planning to do during Block 2?
questions.help: 2-3 maintenance-only is the recommendation, same as Block 1.

questions.label: Unmanaged high blood pressure (resting > 160/100, not currently treated)?
Are you recovering from COVID and still have elevated resting HR or exercise intolerance?
Have you ever fainted, blacked out, or had unexplained cardiac symptoms during exertion?
Do you take a beta-blocker or other heart-rate-lowering medication?
questions.help: These lower your heart rate at every effort. They don't make training unsafe — but they make heart-rate targets unreachable and heart-rate retests unreadable, so we need to know.

questions.label: Are you pregnant?
questions.help: We ask because heart-rate zones stop being reliable in pregnancy — the guidance in this program is built on them.

questions.label: I understand this program is not medical advice. I'll stop and seek a clinician if I develop chest pain, unexplained dizziness, or a joint issue worsens under load.

physical_tests.label: Resting heart rate — morning average
physical_tests.instructions: For 3 mornings in the intake week, before caffeine, measure HR for 60 seconds. Record the average.

physical_tests.label: 5-minute submax HR at chosen easy pace
physical_tests.instructions: On your goal modality, warm up 5 min, then hold a comfortable, conversational pace for 5 minutes. Record HR at the end. Same pace used at retest — write it down.

physical_tests.label: 20-minute threshold test — sustained hard effort
physical_tests.instructions: Warm up 15 min including 3×30s pickups. Hold the hardest pace / power you can sustain for exactly 20 minutes. Record avg pace / power / avg HR. This becomes your threshold anchor for the block.

physical_tests.label: 2K row time trial — optional
physical_tests.instructions: Only if goal modality is rowing. Warm up 15 min. Row 2K as fast as you can sustain. Record time in seconds. Rest 48h from any hard session.

physical_tests.label: 5K run time trial — optional
physical_tests.instructions: Only if goal modality is running AND joints allow it. Warm up 15 min including 2×30s pickups. Run 5K on a flat GPS-measured route. Record time in seconds.

consent.label: I understand this is a training template, not medical advice. I'll consult a clinician for any joint issue that worsens under load, chest pain, or unexplained shortness of breath.
I consent to storing my logged symptoms and training metrics locally in this app.

safety_gates.block_body: Block 2 stacks two hard sessions per week on top of a Z1 volume floor. Without the aerobic base Block 1 (or an equivalent) builds, this block will over-fatigue you and under-adapt. Start with Engine Builder Block 1.
The threshold and Norwegian 4×4 sessions push HR near max. Unmanaged hypertension makes that unsafe. Get BP treated before starting.
History of exertional syncope or unexplained cardiac symptoms is a full-clearance prerequisite before any high-intensity program.

safety_gates.block_title: Wait for baseline HR to normalise
safety_gates.block_body: Persistent HR elevation post-COVID means the cardiovascular system is still recovering. Interval work now can prolong recovery.

safety_gates.block_title: Heart-rate targets won't apply to you
safety_gates.block_body: Beta-blockers and similar medications lower your heart rate at every effort level. The HR zones and the 90-95%-of-max targets in this program will be unreachable, and the heart-rate retest will read as no progress even when you're improving. Train by perceived effort and pace instead, and treat the HR numbers as decoration.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll go by effort and pace, not heart rate.

safety_gates.block_body: You said you're not sure. The easy work here is fine either way — the concern is the threshold and interval work from week 1. A pharmacy cuff takes two minutes. Get a reading before then, and see a clinician if it's high.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: I'll get a reading before the hard sessions start.

safety_gates.block_title: Heart-rate zones won't be reliable for you
safety_gates.block_body: Resting and working heart rate both shift in pregnancy, so the zone targets and the submax-HR retest won't mean what they normally mean. Train by perceived effort, and take the programming to your midwife or clinician rather than to an app.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll go by effort and talk to my clinician.

plan_tiers.label: Foundation
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8-12: threshold pace shifts 2-4%, submax HR at intake pace drops 3-6 bpm, VO2max +4-7%. If you re-entered after a lapse, the 2-week ramp catches you up.

program_adjustments.note: Foundation tier adds a 2-week re-entry ramp before the main progression, delays the first Norwegian 4×4 to week 5, and shortens the threshold expansion (3×8 → 3×12 instead of 3×15). Total block length becomes 10-12 weeks.

plan_tiers.label: Progression
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8-10: threshold pace shifts 3-5%, submax HR drops 5-8 bpm, VO2max +6-9%. This is the reference tier — Block 1 into Block 2 is the assumed path.

program_adjustments.note: Progression is the reference plan. Weekly template runs as written. 8-week block; extension to 10-12 weeks optional if the user wants more before Block 3.

plan_tiers.label: Push
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 8-10: threshold pace shifts 4-6%, submax HR drops 5-10 bpm, VO2max +4-8% (ceiling effect for well-adapted users). Adds a third weekly hard session as an optional Z3/threshold cruise from week 5.

program_adjustments.note: Push scales Z1 durations by ~15%, unlocks a third optional hard session from week 5 (short-interval or tempo), and pushes the threshold ceiling to 3×18 min. Not recommended for anyone below a HERITAGE-style high-responder — Ross 2015 shows dose is usually the fix for apparent non-response, but the ceiling for VO2max in Block 2 is real.

phases.name: Weeks 1-2 — Re-entry ramp (Foundation tier only)
phases.goal: Two weeks of Z1 volume + one sustained tempo per week. Rebuild the base before layering intensity.
phases.template_note: Only fires for Foundation tier (block_1_completed == 'yes_lapsed' or 'no_but_equivalent' with low volume). Progression and Push tiers skip this phase and start at phase_1_intro_week.

phases.name: Week 1 — Baseline check + first threshold
phases.goal: Establish or confirm the 20-min threshold anchor. One 3×8 threshold session at the anchor pace. Two Z1 sessions.
phases.template_note: If the user did the 20-min TT at intake within the last week, this week uses that number. Otherwise a fresh 20-min TT lands Wednesday.
notes: If HR won't hold at threshold on the 3×8, the intake number was too aggressive — engine proposes recalibrating.
First threshold session is intentionally moderate — the ramp lives ahead.

phases.name: Weeks 2-3 — Threshold expansion + first Norwegian 4×4
phases.goal: Threshold expands from 3×8 → 3×10 minutes. First Norwegian 4×4 of the block lands week 2 (Progression / Push) or week 3 (Foundation).
phases.template_note: Two hard sessions per week from week 2. Non-negotiable: 48h between the two.
notes: Volume: Z1 sessions at 60-75 min for Progression, +15% for Push, -15% for Foundation.
If the 4×4 HR fails to reach 90% max on set 1, engine proposes swapping in a threshold cruise instead — high-intensity fails on under-recovery.

phases.name: Week 4 — Short-interval variant + threshold hold
phases.goal: The VO2max session becomes short-interval (5×3 min or 8×2 min) this week — accumulates more time-at-VO2max per session (Ronnestad & Hansen 2020).
phases.template_note: Alternating the format weeks 4-8 is the block's variety mechanism. Threshold stays at 3×10 this week.
notes: Short intervals feel harder set-to-set than 4×4 despite lower absolute duration — expect this.

phases.name: Weeks 5-6 — Threshold to 3×12, back to 4×4
phases.goal: Threshold expands to 3×12 minutes. VO2max session returns to 4×4 for these two weeks.
phases.template_note: Peak-volume window. Z1 volume floor +15% vs week 1 for Progression tier; +30% for Push.
notes: This is where the concurrent-strength interference bites hardest (Fyfe 2016 volume-driven interference). Lower the RPE cap to 6.5 if any lift feels 8+.

phases.name: Week 7 — Short-interval + optional Z3 (Push tier)
phases.goal: Short intervals return. Threshold stays at 3×12. Push tier optionally adds a third hard session (Z3 tempo).
phases.template_note: Push tier only adds the third session — Progression stays at two hard sessions.
notes: Foundation tier drops one Z1 this week to absorb the second short-interval session in place of a threshold. Total sessions stay at 4.

phases.name: Week 8 — Threshold to 3×15, final VO2max stimulus
phases.goal: Threshold hits the block's ceiling (3×15 for Progression, 3×18 for Push, 3×12 for Foundation). VO2max session is the last 4×4 of the block.
phases.template_note: Final stimulus week before the taper.
notes: If the threshold session degrades across sets — HR climbs but pace/power drops — engine flags that the block ceiling is reached. Don't push into red.

phases.name: Weeks 9-10 (or 8) — Taper and retest
phases.goal: One week reduced volume, one week retest. Repeat the intake protocol at retest — 20-min TT, submax HR at fixed pace, resting HR, plus modality-specific TT (2K row / 5K run).
phases.test_at_end: Retest 20-min TT + submax HR at intake pace + resting HR (3 mornings). Delta is the Block 2 outcome.
phases.template_note: Mujika & Padilla 2000 taper literature: intensity preserved, volume down 40-60%, session count -1. The last 3 days before the retest are Z1 only.
notes: Retest wants 48h from any hard session and 24h from any strength session.
Block 3 (polarised) picks up 1-2 weeks after Block 2 ends. Do NOT go straight from retest into another hard block — the taper preserved the fitness; a rest week uses it.

blocks.name: Zone 1/2 steady-state
blocks.note: Modality declared at intake. Z1 volume floor rises across the block. See weekly template for duration by week and tier.

items.scheme: Duration set by week + tier — see weekly template.

blocks.name: Sustained tempo — sub-threshold cruise
blocks.note: Sub-threshold sustained work at 83-88% HRmax / 88-94% FTP. Fills the middle intensity slot for Foundation tier and the optional third session for Push tier.

items.scheme: 20-35 minutes at sub-threshold. Week 1: 20 min. Weeks 3-8: 25-35 min.

blocks.name: Threshold cruise intervals (primary Block 2 driver)
blocks.note: 12-15 min warm up including 3×30s pickups → interval set at ~90-92% HRmax → 8-10 min cool down. This is the block's headline session. Duration ceiling rises across the block.

items.scheme: Progression tier: 3×8 (W1) → 3×10 (W2-4) → 3×12 (W5-7) → 3×15 (W8). Push: ceiling 3×18. Foundation: ceiling 3×12.

blocks.name: Norwegian 4×4 VO2max intervals
blocks.note: 12-15 min warm up including 3×30s pickups → 4×[4 min @ 90-95% HRmax / 3 min active recovery] → 8-10 min cool down. Non-negotiable: 48h clear both sides.

items.scheme: 4 sets × 4 min at 90-95% HRmax, 3 min active recovery. Alternates with block_short_intervals across the block.

substitutions.if_hr_won't_climb_on_set_1: Bail out to Z1 easy for 30 min. Reschedule with 48h clear.
substitutions.if_last_two_sets_pace_drops: Cap at 3 sets next time this session comes up. Under-recovered.

blocks.name: Short-interval VO2max (5×3 or 8×2)
blocks.note: Rønnestad & Hansen 2020 short-interval format. More time-at-VO2max per session than 4×4 for well-trained users, less monotony, higher perceived recoverability.

items.scheme: 5×3 min at 92-95% HRmax with 2 min recovery, OR 8×2 min at 95%+ HRmax with 1 min recovery. Pick one per session; alternate weekly.

blocks.name: Optional Z3 tempo (Push tier third hard session)
blocks.note: Push tier only. Unlocks from week 5. A 20-30 min continuous Z3 tempo (roughly 82-87% HRmax). Extra time-in-zone without the recovery cost of a fourth threshold.

items.scheme: 20-30 min continuous at Z3. Placement: mid-week between the two primary hard sessions. 6+ h separation from any strength.

blocks.name: Easy recovery flush
blocks.note: Very easy pace, HR under 65% max. Blood flow, not adaptation. Appears in the taper week and any peak-volume week where a fifth session helps recovery.

blocks.name: 20-min TT — baseline or retest
blocks.note: Fresh 20-min all-out effort. Sets the block's threshold anchor at week 1 (if not done at intake) and retests at week 4 (mid-block check) and end-of-block. Same modality every time.

items.scheme: 15 min warm up including 3×30s pickups, 20 min hard sustained, 5-10 min cool down. Record avg pace / power / HR.

weekly_template.note: Reference layout for Progression tier. Push adds a third hard session; Foundation drops one Z1 and delays first 4×4. Sessions on non-consecutive days when possible; 48h between the two hard sessions is non-negotiable.

layout.note: Mid-block retest — optional if you'd rather keep the day as recovery. Push tier: mandatory.

placement_principles: Never place hard sessions on consecutive days.
48+ h between the threshold session and the VO2max session in the same week.
24+ h between any hard cardio and any concurrent strength session; 6+ h if same day.
Push tier third hard session (Z3): only mid-week, 6+ h from primary hard sessions.
If life forces skipping, drop the last Z1 first — never the threshold.
Foundation tier: skip the Norwegian 4×4 in weeks 2-3 if HR won't hit target; use threshold cruise instead. First 4×4 lands week 5.

progression_rules.assessment_note: Judge by next-morning HR + subjective recovery. Threshold retest at week 4 is the mid-block adjustment point.

states.label: Hold — swap a hard for Z1 OR shorten by 20%

conditions.or: life_load 7+ or sleep < 6h two nights running

progression_rules.week_end_rule: If the week's threshold session hit target pace/power AND ended feeling like you had one more interval → proceed. If threshold degraded across sets → hold at current volume next week. Two consecutive weeks of threshold regression → engine proposes swapping one 4×4 for a threshold cruise the following week.
progression_rules.escalation: Two red days in the same week → skip the VO2max session that week; do threshold + Z1 only. Three red days in a row → take a full week off before returning.

daily_log_schema.derived_state_rule: red if morning_rhr > baseline + 10 OR new_joint_pain OR illness_symptoms; amber if rhr 5-10 above baseline OR life_load >= 7; else green

immediate_actions.action: If you haven't done a 20-min TT in the last 4 weeks, put it on week 1 Wednesday and don't skip it.
immediate_actions.reason: Block 2's whole progression targets threshold. Without a baseline, the interval prescriptions run on best-guess numbers.

immediate_actions.action: Buy or borrow a chest-strap HR monitor for the block if you don't have one.
immediate_actions.reason: Wrist-optical HR is unreliable at threshold and above. Half the block's target zones sit in the range where optical drops out.

immediate_actions.action: Decide the maintenance strength plan BEFORE week 1 and write down the 2-3 sessions you'll do.
immediate_actions.reason: Block 2's volume is where concurrent-training interference bites hardest (Fyfe 2016). Ad-hoc lifting during peak-volume weeks 5-7 undoes half the aerobic gain.

immediate_actions.action: Set week-8 (or week-10 for Foundation) retest on the calendar now. Book the Thursday.
immediate_actions.reason: The retest is the block's proof of work. Skipping it makes Block 3 planning guesswork.

physiological_targets: Threshold (LT2 / MLSS) pace / power shift +2-5% over 8-12 weeks — the biggest single lever for 20-90 min endurance performance (Joyner & Coyle 2008). Driven by MCT1 upregulation (Pilegaard 2000), mitochondrial density in Type I fibres (Bishop 2019), and crossover-point shift (Brooks & Mercier 1994).

VO2max +4-9% additional gain on top of Block 1 outcomes — decreasing marginal returns; the base delivered most, Block 2 adds more. Astorino 2013 short-HIIT data + Helgerud 2007 Norwegian 4×4 data anchor the range.

Time-at-VO2max per week +50-100% vs Block 1 — Block 2's two hard sessions accumulate more time-at-VO2max than Block 1's one. Buchheit & Laursen 2013 (parts A + B) frame time-at-VO2max as the primary driver of the peak-capacity end of the aerobic system.

Mitochondrial content plateaus but oxidative-enzyme activity keeps climbing — Konopka 2014 12-week data shows β-HAD +397-435% at week 12 (already showing at week 8 in Block 1). Additional gains here compound.
Stroke volume adaptation continues — Helgerud 2007 (+10% SV) + Wisløff 2007 (+35% LV EF in HF patients) anchor. Block 2's two hard sessions sustain the cardiac remodelling stimulus.

session_rationale.block_z1_steady: Same rationale as Block 1 — the volume floor is what makes the intensity above it sustainable. Bishop 2019: volume drives mitochondrial content. Block 2 leans on Block 1's base and expands.
session_rationale.block_sustained_tempo: Sub-threshold work drives MCT1 (Pilegaard 2000) and shifts crossover (Brooks & Mercier 1994). Used in Foundation-tier re-entry and Push-tier third-session slot.
session_rationale.block_threshold_cruise: Block 2's primary driver. LT2 shift is the biggest performance lever for the target duration range (Joyner & Coyle 2008). The 3×8 → 3×15 expansion mirrors coaching-consensus threshold blocks (Seiler 2010 polarised model's threshold zone). Rønnestad 2020 long-vs-short interval comparison: long intervals produce comparable adaptation with less monotony.
session_rationale.block_norwegian_4x4: Helgerud 2007 anchor. Time-at-VO2max is the specific driver. Block 2 uses it every other week rather than every week (Rønnestad 2020: short intervals alternated with long intervals maintain adaptation with less staleness).
session_rationale.block_short_intervals: Rønnestad & Hansen 2020: short-interval format (5×3 or 8×2) accumulates more time-at-VO2max per session for well-trained users. Bishop 2008 repeated-sprint literature supports short-interval work as VO2max complement. Alternated with 4×4 to keep the stimulus varied.
session_rationale.block_z3_optional_push: Push tier only. Extra time-in-zone (~82-87% HRmax, sub-threshold) without the recovery cost of a fourth hard session. Buchheit & Laursen 2013 threshold-zone rationale.
session_rationale.block_easy_recovery: Blood flow at Z1 (60-70% HRmax) accelerates lactate clearance and glycogen replenishment vs complete rest. Used in taper.
session_rationale.block_20min_tt_or_confirm: 20-min TT as threshold anchor. Coggan's FTP protocol convention (widely used in cycling; adapted for row / ski / run). Rest HR + submax HR are equipment-independent baselines; the 20-min TT is the modality-specific one.

evidence_base.progression_rationale: Block 2 leans on Block 1's base. Week 1 confirms or sets the 20-min threshold anchor. Weeks 2-3 layer the first Norwegian 4×4 on top of one threshold session per week (Rønnestad 2020 style: two hard sessions/wk is the well-supported dose). Week 4 swaps in short-interval format (Rønnestad & Hansen 2020) plus mid-block retest. Weeks 5-6 expand threshold to 3×12 and return to 4×4. Week 7 alternates short-interval again (variety avoids staleness — Buchheit & Laursen 2013). Week 8 hits the ceiling (3×15 threshold + last 4×4). Weeks 9-10 taper + retest (Mujika & Padilla 2000 taper literature: intensity preserved, volume down 40-60%). Concurrent-strength policy tightens in weeks 5-7 as volume peaks (Fyfe 2016 endurance-volume-driven interference). Foundation tier adds a 2-week re-entry ramp before the main progression, delaying the first 4×4 to week 5.
evidence_base.outcome_evidence: Effect-size expectations synthesised for a user who completed Block 1 (or has an equivalent base). Threshold pace / power +2-5% (Progression tier), +3-6% (Push), +2-4% (Foundation). Submax HR at fixed pace additional -3 to -8 bpm on top of Block 1 gains. VO2max additional +5-10% (Progression), +4-8% (Push, ceiling effect), +4-7% (Foundation). 2K row TT: additional 3-8s improvement. 5K run TT: 2-4% improvement. Individual variation is large — HERITAGE (Bouchard 1999) ~10× range in gains under identical prescription. Non-response usually resolves at higher intensity (Ross 2015 — but Block 2 is already at the intensity cap; if the response is thin here, Block 3's polarised shift is the next lever). Direct RCT precedent for a Block-2-shaped protocol: Ronnestad & Hansen 2020 (12 weeks, two hard sessions/wk); Astorino 2013 (VO2max HIIT dose-response); Helgerud 2007 (Norwegian 4×4).
contraindications: Unmanaged hypertension (BP > 160/100 at rest) — Block 2's hard sessions are more frequent than Block 1's. Get BP treated before starting.
First-trimester pregnancy — HR-based zones are unreliable during pregnancy; work with a specialist.
Any joint or tendon condition that flares under load — reconsider the running variant if applicable.
Post-COVID convalescence with persistent resting HR elevation — do not begin. Return when baseline HR is back.
History of exertional syncope or unexplained cardiac symptoms — full clearance first.
Insufficient aerobic base (< 4 hrs/week for the last 4 weeks AND no Block 1 completion) — the intake gate fires; run Block 1 first.
evidence_base.adaptive_engine_hooks: Morning resting HR is the primary daily signal — >10 bpm above baseline gates the day's hard session to Z1 automatically (proposal, user Accepts). Two consecutive weeks of threshold session regression → engine proposes swapping one 4×4 for a threshold cruise the following week (block flags under-recovery pattern). If the threshold session degrades across sets in a single week (HR climbs but pace/power drops set-over-set), engine proposes shortening the next threshold to the last successfully completed volume (e.g. cap 3×12 if 3×15 fell apart). Life-load score of 7+ mid-week combined with a missed session prompts a Z1 substitution on the hard day. If a hard cardio session lands within 6 hours of a lifting session, engine proposes moving one — Robineau 2016 6h separation threshold. Mid-block retest (week 4) triggers a proposal to hold/advance threshold pace targets. All adjustments respect confirm-first.
engineering_choices_flagged: Threshold expansion 3×8 → 3×15 min across 8 weeks — mirrors coaching-consensus threshold blocks (Seiler-adjacent), not a specific RCT-derived progression.
Alternating 4×4 and short-interval formats week-by-week — Rønnestad 2020 supports both formats but doesn't specify weekly alternation as the optimum.
Z3 optional third session for Push tier — pragmatic; Buchheit & Laursen 2013 support the zone but not the exact placement.
20-min TT as threshold anchor — widely used FTP protocol convention, not a specific RCT.
Foundation-tier 2-week re-entry ramp — engineering choice; Coyle 1984 detraining timecourse informs the concept but not the exact protocol.
Week 4 mid-block retest — coach-consensus mid-block check, not RCT-derived cadence.
Z1 volume floor +30% by week 5-6 (Progression) — pragmatic; Bishop 2019 supports volume beyond a threshold but exact percentage is engineering choice.
48h between the two hard sessions — supported by multiple ITT-style recovery studies but not specifically threshold-vs-VO2max.
10% weekly mileage cap for runners — Nielsen 2014 injury dose-response supports the direction but the exact 10% is coaching folklore.
evidence_base.hr_zone_methodology: Same as Block 1: HRmax from HUNT formula (211 − 0.64 × age) per Nes 2013 as default; observed HRmax from a hard interval session preferred. Zone floors set as %HRR (Karvonen 1957) rather than %HRmax. Threshold zone: 88-92% HRmax / 90-94% FTP / 82-88% VDOT. DFA a1 = 0.75 as VT1 anchor per Rogers 2021 for chest-strap owners.
evidence_base.concurrent_strength_prescription: Same rules as Block 1, tightened. Block 2 is where the volume-driven interference (Fyfe 2016) bites hardest. RPE ≤ 7, 2-3 sessions/week, no explosive PR attempts (Schumann 2022 SMD -0.28 on explosive strength). Lift first if same day (Eddens 2018 +6.91%). 6+ h separation preferred (Robineau 2016). Protein floor 1.6 g/kg/day (Morton 2018). Fuel resistance sessions (Impey 2018 'Fuel for the Work Required'). Skip lower-body strength within 24 h of a Norwegian 4×4.

onboarding_steps.title: The 0-10 scale
onboarding_steps.body_md: Block 2 pushes closer to the top-end of your recovery capacity. Rate readiness honestly each morning — this is where the confirm-first proposals earn their keep.

anchors.low: Fresh, ready for the hard session
anchors.mid: Gritty but functional — hold as written
anchors.high: Cooked — swap the hard session for Z1

onboarding_steps.title: Life load, today
onboarding_steps.body_md: Two hard sessions per week means the buffer is thinner. Block 2 uses your life-load rating to propose swaps before the block runs you into over-reach.

onboarding_steps.title: How Engine Builder Block 2 works
onboarding_steps.body_md: Two hard sessions a week — a threshold cruise + a VO2max session that alternates 4×4 and short-interval formats. Two to three Z1 sessions frame them. The block's headline metric is threshold pace / power shift, not VO2max. Retest at week 4 and end-of-block. If you didn't complete Block 1 (or an equivalent base), start there instead — this block assumes it.
